reading.body:
H.R. 7066 is a Democratic-only bill aimed at electricity costs from large loads, with one sponsor and fourteen cosponsors and no lobbying filings naming it since 2025.

The bill's title ties rising electricity demand to large loads, and its tagged issues are energy and data centers. That pairing is the whole substance of the record here: a legislative vehicle that treats data center power draw as a cost problem to be addressed, introduced by a member and co-signed entirely within one party. The absence of any recorded vote in the data means the bill's position in the process is not visible from this page.

The lobbying count is the most informative number. Zero filings for 2025 or later name the bill, which means no outside interest has registered it as an issue in disclosed lobbying during that window. A bill that touches data center power and has attracted no named lobbying activity is either early, low-profile, or both. The data cannot distinguish those cases.

What the data does not cover: the bill's text, its committee referral, any hearing or vote, and any position taken by the cosponsors beyond signing on. It also does not show utility, grid operator, or hyperscaler spending on the underlying issue, only filings that name this specific bill. The link between this legislation and actual interconnection or siting outcomes is not established here.
